sourceFindings.finding: Server wraps returned EvalResponse in CmdSuccess. A transport/command success can carry eval success=false. CLI observed Windows unwraps to data.result eval DTO. Check process exit, outer success/errors, exact target/bound command+parameters, inner typed success, diagnostic errors, and user-return phase receipt separately; HTTP200/outertrue is insufficient.

Lean mode strips command/executedAt/executionTime metadata on nested BaseResponse objects, drops null error/message keys and failure result; successful result stays present even null. output/diagnostics are DTO payload; optional warning/busy/dialog/argument fields can appear. Do not require exactly four total fields or require lean metadata. Keep full raw response. EvalSuccess/EvalFailure hardcode inner Command="eval" even for eval_file; do not require inner command=eval_file. Verify bound CLI command/parameters/target separately.

eval accepts inline code; eval_file takes file. eval_file checks nonempty path, case-insensitive.cs extension, existence/readability/nonempty content and then same EvaluateSource. File read happens on Unity side; relative path resolves Unity process cwd, not CLI shell/--project-path. Use an exact owned absolute path on target machine, raw hash before/after; no canonicalization/reparse guard is supplied by eval_file itself.

File content is embedded as method body in generated static Execute with limited using directives; not a full compilation unit. Explicit return supplies user-result; absent return yields null. JSON-returned strings remain strings, other objects are serialized to JSON-compatible values. Do not scrape Debug.Log or output for phase success.

Compilation failure includes diagnostics. Successful compiler path does not pass collected compilation diagnostics into EvalSuccess; empty diagnostics is not proof of no warnings. ExecuteCompiledAssembly does not set Output; output may be null even if code logs elsewhere. Exception detail is carried as runtime/execution error; returned false/failed payload does not itself throw, so validate its schema.

eval parameter timeout defaults5000ms, accepted1..86400000ms. Server exec timeout is milliseconds; CLI global timeout is seconds per skill. Binding collision/forwarding not executed locally: inspect actual echoed parameters, never assume one flag controls both. Dispatcher uses requested eval wait budget except detached-job unbounded lane. Queued cancellation only; once started TryCancel is no-op. Eval compiler passes timeoutMs into a method that does not use it to cancel compilation/execution. Timeout/disconnect is not proof of rollback or disarm; no automatic ARM retry.

Each eval generates a fresh GUID-derived assembly/type and loads it into memory. Editor references existing loaded non-dynamic assemblies with known paths, skipping failures; does not prove exact build/RSP identity or native compiler consumption. eval is not an installed project owner or native validation substitute.

sourceFindings.related: Microsoft Delegate equality and event unsubscribe documentation in references.json
sourceFindings.finding: Inference from fresh assembly/type plus delegate identity semantics: ARM lambda/localfunction defined in that eval and identical-text DISARM lambda compiled by later eval do not identify the same method/target. This concern does not apply to eval forwarding to the SAME existing stable compiled named-method owner or retrieving the exact saved delegate object from such an owner within same domain. A compiled owner is not mandatory if AppDomain.GetData returns the ORIGINAL System.Action retained by ARM; invoking that exact closure can unsubscribe its captured original delegates despite a fresh eval wrapper. AppDomain data is domain-local and does not establish cross-reload continuity.

Installed package demonstrates compiled InitializeOnLoad bootstrap, durable pre-reload persistence and named -=/+= hooks. This is a pattern, not permission to modify it. Existing stable reviewed owner should retain exact delegate/owner token and report idempotent subscriptions; same-text fresh eval callbacks are insufficient. No proposed Windows observer code inspected, so its callback owner classification remains pending. This compiled bootstrap pattern is one option, not a requirement for a same-domain stored-closure observer. Windows reports its actual observer uses AppDomain exact original Stop and promises no after-reload continuation.

windowsObserverOwnership.pattern: ARM stores ORIGINAL Stop closure as System.Action under unique AppDomain.CurrentDomain key. DISARM GetData casts/invokes existing Action. Original Stop captures exact event delegates, removes them, clears slot, writes Disarmed and disposes writer. ARM rejects reused key. beforeAssemblyReload calls that same Stop.
windowsObserverOwnership.sourceAssessment: Reported pattern is compatible with exact stored-delegate option in SAME AppDomain and avoids reconstructing fresh eval lambdas. Actual observer is NOT classified as broken. Pattern/source report is not executed control acceptance.
windowsObserverOwnership.crossReloadScope: No after-real-reload continuation promised. Old AppDomain slot/delegates must not be assumed available in new domain.
